tldr: This position paper advocates for formal mathematical reasoning, grounded in proof assistants like Lean, as an indispensable complementary approach to informal LLM-based methods for advancing AI4Math beyond high school-level mathematics.
contributions: Critically examines limitations of the informal approach (data scarcity and lack of correctness verifiability in advanced mathematics)
Introduces formal mathematical reasoning and proof assistants as a solution to these challenges
Summarizes existing progress in theorem proving and autoformalization
Identifies open challenges in data and algorithms
Proposes milestones for measuring AI's capabilities in formal mathematical reasoning
Calls on the research community to drive transformative advancements
methods: This is a position paper that reviews and synthesizes existing research rather than presenting new experiments. It analyzes the informal approach to AI4Math using NuminaMath (which solved 29 out of 50 AIMO test problems) as a case study of state-of-the-art math LLMs. It then introduces formal mathematical reasoning through proof assistants (Lean, Coq, Isabelle) and describes the common architecture of neural theorem provers combining tactic generation and proof search. It references AlphaProof, which used autoformalization combined with reinforcement learning to achieve IMO silver medal level.
results: The number of publications in formal mathematical reasoning nearly doubled in 2023 and is projected to double again in 2024. AlphaProof became the first AI to achieve IMO silver medal level. Autoformalization has reached a point where it can bootstrap neural theorem prover capabilities. Lean has gained popularity among mathematicians, leading to formalized research mathematics and general-purpose libraries like mathlib. Multilingual infrastructures for Coq and Isabelle are beginning to be built. LLMs can assist human mathematicians in writing formal proofs, potentially initiating a data flywheel. The informal approach remains limited mostly to high school math not exceeding AIME level.
limitations: Data scarcity: High-quality training data is scarce in advanced mathematics, and novel research problems make data collection infeasible
Lack of correctness verifiability: LLMs hallucinate plausible reasoning steps, and intrinsic self-verification remains an open question
Scaling up the informal approach during training alone cannot resolve these challenges
Advanced mathematics frequently involves abstract conjectures and proofs that resist numeric evaluation
Formal verification has historically been too costly to deploy broadly
Self-verification approaches with LLMs have yielded mixed results
